item.title: Lint, simulate, test
item.description:
Three checks, in the order you reach for them.

Lint

tik lint processes/support-request.edn

The linter enforces what the kernel cannot:

  • The closed guard basis — only operators the declared :process/guard-vocab admits.
  • Graph sanity — every :after names a stage that exists, and no cycles.
  • Stratified negation — [:not [:stage-reached …]] may only name a stage in a strictly earlier stratum, which is what makes the fixpoint provably deterministic.
  • Facts over flags — a warning where a bare boolean stands in for information worth recording.
  • Prefix boundaries — an :artifact prefix that does not end at a path boundary matches more than its author expects.

With no argument it lints the store instead: open tickets missing descriptions, titles, or signatures.

item.title: Roles and authority
item.description:
A role is a name a definition uses in its guards. Membership is store state that decides who is in that role today.

Declaring a role

:process/roles
{:triager {:members ["seb"]}
 :approver {:members ["alice" "bob"]}}

Guards refer to the name:

:guards [[:signed-by :triager [:category]]]

That guard holds when the fact at [:category] was asserted by a member of :triager. It is a statement about evidence — who put this claim on the record — rather than a permission check performed somewhere else.

item.title: Writing a definition
item.description:
The design law

A stage is defined by what must be TRUE to reach it, never by who moved what. Ask of every stage: what evidence, on record, would convince a sceptical auditor a year from now? Write that as guards. If the honest answer is “somebody said so”, then make that the fact — a named person’s signature on a named claim — rather than a status somebody sets.
